view: This print turns on Old Navy's Q3 comp against the flat-to-down-1 guide and on what the company says about Q4 and holiday under a new Old Navy CEO who started on 11-02. Headline adjusted EPS matters less, because tariff relief (Section 122 at 10% plus mitigation, guided at about 150bp of Q3 gross-margin benefit) and SG&A leverage make an adjusted-EPS beat the base case, as in August. Revenue is the weaker side: management itself pointed to the low end ($4.00B) while the Street models $4.02B to $4.05B. The fresh industry data is mixed. Census clothing-store sales rose 4.7% YoY over Aug-Oct, the same pace as in Q2, which is when Gap comped -1%. October slowed (+3.1% YoY, down m/m SA after +5.75% in September). Target's apparel sales fell 3.8% YoY in a quarter where its total comp rose 5.6%, and that is Old Navy's closest value-family rival. TJX comped +4% against a 2-3% plan, so value shoppers were spending, but at off-price. Against that, the stock has de-rated about 20 points against XRT over a month and now trades below its pre-Q2 level with no identified news. The bar has dropped, and an in-line quarter with the FY EPS range held (which still beats the $2.33 FY consensus) could pop the way August did. The risk is that the slide reflects card or traffic data showing an October Old Navy miss, or that the new Old Navy chief resets holiday expectations. I cannot tell which of these the price holds, so I have no direction.

recommendation.reason: Both sides are live and neither is unpriced in a way I can show. Upside: a likely adjusted-EPS beat and an FY range above consensus, while the stock has given back its whole Q2 pop. Downside: revenue at the low end against a Street midpoint, soft October apparel, Target apparel -3.8%, and a new Old Navy CEO who could reset the holiday guide. The month-long name-specific slide lowers the bar but has no identified cause, so I cannot say whether it is informed selling or sentiment.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: An Old Navy Q3 comp of flat or positive with the FY EPS range held or raised would make this a clear up move. An Old Navy comp worse than -2% or a cut to the FY sales or EPS guide would make it a down move of mid-teens size.

self_critique: A sharp name-specific slide into a print with no news is often the mark of alternative-data funds front-running a miss. If so, a weak Old Navy number plus a cautious holiday guide from the new chief could still drive a mid-teens drop, as in March and May. The other way round, I may be underweighting how reliably Gap beats adjusted EPS and how violently a de-rated, moderately shorted stock squeezes on in-line news, as in August's +13% on a sales miss. Neither case is strong enough to move me off about 50.
approach_notes: Writing down the guide against consensus first (P2 step 1) and rebuilding EPS from the guide paid; the counterparty-first search (Target apparel, TJX) gave the only fresh demand traces. Alt-data searches (P3 physical/worker) came back empty for this name and cost time without moving the view.
